Confusable pairs among the license withdrawal grounds, followed by continuation facts; each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A01
You can get a copy of your own driving record from the state's online DVS service. [A01]
Why it matters: group driving record; the web address is a dynamic detail.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A01
Allowing someone else to take any part of the license exam for you is a suspension ground, just like taking it for someone else. [A01]
Why it matters: group fraud grounds; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A01
Even one misdemeanor conviction for breaking a Minnesota traffic law is listed as a possible ground for suspension. [A01]
Why it matters: group suspension grounds; confusable with the more serious revocation grounds; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A02
Reinstatement after a suspension has requirements that include paying the reinstatement fee, while reinstatement after a revocation requires meeting every item on the withdrawal notice, testing with proper identification, and applying for a new license. [A02]
Why it matters: group reinstatement; confusable suspension versus revocation steps; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A02
A traffic offense in another state can count toward revocation in Minnesota when it would be grounds for revocation if committed here. [A02]
Why it matters: group out-of-state offenses; links to the matching suspension ground.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A02
A misdemeanor conviction for driving while knowing the vehicle's owner lacked no-fault insurance is a revocation ground. [A02]
Why it matters: group insurance grounds; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A03
The core test for cancellation is whether you have a legal right to the license issued to you, though cancellation can also be the legal punishment for certain crimes. [A03]
Why it matters: group withdrawal types; confusable cancellation versus the other two; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A03
A limited license is available only to some drivers whose privileges were suspended or revoked, never as a general license, and its trips are restricted to the listed purposes. [A03]
Why it matters: group limited license; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec13-R09 | anchor: A03
Commercial driver's license holders can lose those privileges for certain driving offenses, and the Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual covers those rules. [A03]
Why it matters: group commercial licenses; outside the Class D test focus.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0093]
